newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Sing Tao says to shut evening newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Sing Tao says to shut evening newspaper.

text.p: Sing Tao Holdings Ltd will stop publishing the Sing Tao Evening Post newspaper from December 18 after drops in both circulation and advertising revenue, the group said in a statement on Tuesday.
The majority of employees will be laid off, it said, while about 10 percent would be transfered to other departments within the Sing Tao group. It did not specify the size of the layoffs.
"In recent years, due to the shrinking of the evening newspaper market, the Sing Tao Evening Post reported a drop both in circulation and advertising revenue," Sing Tao said.
Sing Tao said it estimates the group will cut losses by almost HK$50 million a year by closing the evening paper, which was founded in 1938.

"After reviewing the overall development of the Sing Tao Evening Post and accepting the forecast that the business will not improve, the board of directors of Sing Tao Holdings Ltd decided to suspended the publication of the Sing Tao Evening Post," it said.

Six months ago, the newspaper carried out a major overhaul of staffing and content. The move stablised circulation at 20,000 copies per day but there was no increase in advertising revenue and the losses continued, Sing Tao said.
The group's other businesses will not be affected, it said.
Trading of Sing Tao shares was suspended at the company's request on Tuesday morning.
